channel.description: JavaScript from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Next.js 16.3 Released
item.description: Next.js 16.3 introduces Instant Navigations, a suite of tools for single-page-app responsiveness, plus a faster dev server, faster builds, and improved tooling for AI agents. (1 source: javascriptweekly)

item.title: Google Releases Angular v22 with Stable Signal Forms, OnPush by Default and Experimental WebMCP
item.description: Angular v22, Google's TypeScript-first framework, has introduced API stabilizations, ergonomic templates, and tooling enhancements for AI integration. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Let's Make the Worst htmx Ever
item.description: Learning how htmx works by building one from scratch. (1 source: javascriptweekly)

item.title: Show HN: textlog – A quiet, text-only microblogging platform, open-source, no JS
item.description: A quieter place for your thoughts. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: npm Staged Publishing Available, Adding a Human Approval Step before Packages Go Live
item.description: npm has introduced staged publishing for Node.js, requiring maintainer approval before a version is installable. Versions are queued and must pass a two-factor authentication challenge for release. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: GitHub Hardens npm and Actions Defaults, Drawing Debate over Delays versus Signing
item.description: GitHub consolidated the npm and Actions changes it shipped from March to July 2026 against supply chain attacks, several of which alter defaults rather than add options. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: The Secure Way to Release an npm Package in 2026
item.description: How to protect your npm package from being stolen in a supply chain attack and improve its position in security ratings (1 source: javascriptweekly)

item.title: focus on npm security
item.description: Explore the changes we've shipped across npm and GitHub Actions over the past few months to disrupt supply chain attack techniques and limit their impact. (1 source: javascriptweekly)

item.title: scan every npm package for malware
item.description: As part of our ongoing supply-chain security work, npm is introducing automatic scanning of packages at publish time. This changelog covers what publishers can expect and a new metadata requirement… (1 source: javascriptweekly)
